thread:
jared (oncall): paging: p99 latency just spiked across streaming endpoints, multiple customers reporting stalls. alert shows KV cache eviction rate jumped ~x10. opening thread here to coordinate mitigation.

anya (sre): seeing same. p95 up from 180ms -> 600ms, p99 ~2.4s. streaming stalls aligned with decode-phase timeouts. KV cache miss ratio increased from 3% -> 22% in last 10m.

ops-eli: any recent deploys or config changes to caching or prefill logic?

tanvi (runtime): rolled a small change to prefill aggressiveness an hour ago to optimize cold-starts (reduce decode latency for long contexts). hypothesis: prefill is racing decode and inflating KV entries, causing fragmentation and eviction churn.

anya (sre): confirmed. timeline: prefill change at 1987650200, then slow growth in memory usage, then eviction thrash at ~1987654200 when tail QPS hit a burst.

jared (oncall): customer-impact: cs reports 3 mid-market customers saw streaming stalls; on monitoring, 11% of streams had at least one stall. tagging for priority. @customer-success can you DM affected accounts? :frowning:

customer-success: pinged customers with temporary note: "We're investigating intermittent streaming stalls; engineers are on it." Will escalate if they ask for status.

sre-pager: incident severity candidate: Sev2 if customer impact holds. Recommend immediate mitigations then follow with longer fix.

tanvi (runtime): mitigations we can try now (fast):
- rollback prefill aggressiveness change (safe config toggle)
- raise KV cache max size for the affected pool (temp)
- change eviction policy to avoid LRU thrash (set protection window)
- route streaming requests to fallback model variant with smaller KV footprint

anya (sre): prioritize rollback + raise cache size. rollback is config-only and rehearse is minimal risk. raising cache size will buy time but could increase memory pressure cluster-wide; do it only on the dedicated pool handling streaming.

ops-eli: on it, starting a rollback now: `kubectl set env deploy/runtime PREFILL_AGGRESSIVENESS=0 --namespace=runtime-prod`

infra-bot: Deploy triggered by ops-eli. Job ID: deploy-1987654330.

tanvi (runtime): also increasing cache max entries on stream-pool to +30% (config flip). issuing change: `redwoodctl pools update stream-pool --kv-max-entries=1300000`

infra-bot: pool update accepted. Change ID: pool-1987654334.

anya (sre): monitoring graphs — eviction rate dropping already, miss ratio back to ~8% within 90s. p95 trending down from 600ms -> 260ms. p99 coming down but still high at ~1.1s.

jared (oncall): good. continue to watch for streaming stalls. If stalls persist, we'll do graceful restart of runtime replicas to clear fragmented caches.

tanvi (runtime): a note: fragmentation pattern shows a bunch of medium-sized entries from partial prefill + partial decode. long-lived sessions that prefilled but never completed decode created hot keys. changing eviction threshold to prefer keeping smaller entries helps, but that's more risky.

anya (sre): collect traces from affected requests: `trace-id` samples show heavy time in kv.fetch calls during decode. sending sample logs to thread: ```
[1987654301] stream_id=st-123 kv.fetch keys=124 size=1.2MB duration=320ms
[1987654302] stream_id=st-124 kv.fetch keys=10 size=200KB duration=45ms
[1987654320] stream_id=st-125 decode.read wait_kv=900ms stall=true
```

jared (oncall): nice samples. I'll create an incident ticket and link to docs so we can restore state postmortem. Incident created: INC-198765. severity: S2.

customer-success: updated customers: "We've applied infrastructure mitigations and are monitoring. We'll follow up with root cause within 24 hours."

anya (sre): quick plan for next 2 hours:
1) keep prefill rolled back cluster-wide (done).
2) monitor p50/p95/p99 + eviction metrics every 5m.
3) run a controlled perf test simulating high-concurrency streaming to validate stability.
4) collect heap/allocator profiles from stream pool nodes.

ops-eli: running perf-suite: `./perf/run --scenario streaming-burst --concurrency 600 --duration 10m` and capturing flamegraphs.

infra-bot: perf job started. job-id perf-1987654388.

tanvi (runtime): if perf shows stability, plan is to design a safer prefill ramp: limit prefill per-session, cap total prefill size, and prefer prefill eviction priority lower than decode-generated entries. We'll proposal PR for that.

anya (sre): temporary safeguards to push ASAP:
- set PREFILL_MAX_PER_SESSION=2
- PREFILL_TOTAL_BYTES_CAP=4MB
- eviction protection window 60s for newly-prefilled keys

jared (oncall): can we flip those as feature flags? If so do it now to avoid new thrash.

tanvi (runtime): yes, flags exist. toggling now. `kubectl set env deploy/runtime PREFILL_MAX_PER_SESSION=2 PREFILL_TOTAL_BYTES_CAP=4194304 PREFILL_PROTECT_WINDOW=60`

infra-bot: Flags updated. Change ID: ff-1987654396.

anya (sre): positive signal: p99 dropping into ~700-800ms now and streaming stalls rate down to 2%. eviction rate normalized. Keeping incident open to validate for 1h.

jared (oncall): handoff note for next oncall: incident open INC-198765. mitigations: prefill rolled back, cache size +30% on stream-pool, feature flags set to cap prefill. next steps: run longer perf test, collect heap profiles, design controlled prefill rollout.

jared (oncall): tagging @anya for postmortem lead and @tanvi for runtime fix. I'll update severity if customer impact changes.

anya (sre): will own postmortem. initial RCA hypothesis: prefill aggressiveness change increased transient KV writes that caused fragmentation and eviction thrash under burst, amplifying tail latency for streaming decodes. Need better local quotas and eviction prioritization.

tanvi (runtime): adding to TODOs: implement per-session prefill caps, prefer tiny entry retention, add metrics to track prefill vs decode entry sizes, and smoke test under burst.

jared (oncall): thanks team. continuing to watch. will post final update in 30m or when things fully stabilized. :thumbsup:

sre-pager: auto-note: If any further pages, escalate per oncall runbook.
